newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends mostly down on liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends mostly down on liquidation.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down on Friday due to long liquidation with investors concerned about potential falls in the short term, traders said.
The key November 1996 contract ended at 3,305 yuan ($398) per tonne, losing 37 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 3,327 and hit a low of 3,291.
January fell 40 to 3,185, March 29 to 3,210, May did not trade, July dropped 10 to 3,370 and September rose 99 to 3,380.
Combined volume fell to 9,900 tonnes from 22,100.
Traders said negative technical factors triggered long liquidation with many investors worry about the long-term trend.

"This round of rebound has not changed the long-term downward trend, which makes many investors cautious to follow up," one trader said. "Most of them preferred to liquidate their long positions at high levels."
"Large scale short-covering has pushed the November contract up over the past week after losses of nearly 300 yuan since early October due to over-supply of spot soybean," a second trader said.
"But it did not trigger active sentiment among retail investors," he added.
"Soybean is likely to fall into another downward channel if the 3,300-yuan support level breached," a third trader said.
